svg.title: The original fiber kernels give actual crossed linking corners
svg.desc: Canonical normalized-jet Haar measure, fiber pair convolution, compact Hilbert-module kernels, full reduced crossed linking corners, Banach coefficient bound and the separate still open differential trace transfer. Exact proofs in Lemma 13.29, Proposition 13.30, Corollary 13.31 and Example 13.32.

g.text: The original fiber kernels give actual crossed linking corners
Y = Vₖ → X = V₁. Canonical measure, intrinsic frame action and the exact coefficient norm.
A. Normalized coordinates preserve the fiber Haar density
u′ⱼ = uⱼ + Pⱼ(u₂,…,uⱼ₋₁)
dμₓ = du₂ ··· duₖ
Block-triangular Jacobian; identity diagonal.
Source rotation: uⱼ ↦ R⁻¹uⱼ R⊗ⱼ; orthogonal determinant +1. No invariant section.
B. Pair convolution is actual nilpotent convolution
K(y,z), z = yt
a(y,t) = K(y,yt)
(a*b)(y,t) = ∫ a(y,s)b(ys,s⁻¹t) dμ(s)
ξ(y) ζ̄(z) → θξ,ζ ; finite rank-one closure = K(E)
Eₓ = L²(Yₓ,dμₓ); compact smooth kernels act by the Schur-bound integral.
C. Full reduced linking corners retain every discrete Γ
K(E) ⋊ᵣ Γ
E ⋊ᵣ Γ
Aₓ = C₀(X) ⋊ᵣ Γ
Left corner PCP
Off-diagonal PCQ
Right corner QCQ
‖Ξ a‖ ≤ ‖Ξ‖ ‖a‖Aₓ ≤ ‖Ξ‖ ‖a‖B ; all matrices and external units.
Fullness uses inner products and rank-one spans; the corner projections are Γ-invariant.
D. Compression and the remaining differential trace
eU₁e = eU₋₁e = 0, but eU₁U₋₁e = e ≠ 0: rank-one compression loses products.
Characteristic cycle
Nilpotent cyclic transfer
Controlled trace on B
Still required: a closed differential trace, every inserted-coefficient bound and normalized pairing.
The module multiplication estimate leaves the differential trace clause open.
Proof: (13.99)–(13.104). Context: Connes (1986), Remark 7.16(a). Original argument and diagram.
